title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
abstract: arXiv:2611.23720v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Semantic labels say what a building element is, not what it does: two identical-looking windows on one facade may be operable or fixed, a column may carry load or only decorate. We ask whether 3D point representations encode such architectural function. On 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings with 15 functional attributes per element, we hold out entire buildings and compare hand-crafted descriptors, networks trained from scratch and frozen self-supervised point transformers. Descriptors and frozen features are read by the same linear layer. No network trained from scratch, from PointNet to a 108M-parameter PTv3, clearly exceeds the descriptors (0.610 mAP on functionally ambiguous elements), whereas frozen Utonia reaches 0.732. Random-weight controls of the same architectures (0.649 and 0.652) attribute the gain to pretraining (Utonia: +0.080, 95% building interval [+0.035, +0.124]). Pretrained features improve at every tested number of labelled

translated_title: 三维点表示能否编码建筑功能？基于城市立面探测监督训练与预训练模型
translated_abstract: 语义标签只能说明建筑元素“是什么”，却不能说明它“有何用途”：同一立面上两个外观完全相同的窗户，可能一个是可开启的、另一个是固定的；一根柱子可能承重，也可能仅作装饰。我们探究三维点表示是否能够编码这类建筑功能。在22栋移动激光雷达（LiDAR）扫描的建筑上，每个元素标注15个功能属性，我们以整栋建筑为单位进行留出验证，并比较手工设计的描述子、从头训练的网络以及冻结的自监督点云Transformer。描述子与冻结特征均通过同一个线性层读取。从PointNet到1.08亿参数的PTv3，没有任何从头训练的网络能明显超过手工描述子（在功能模糊元素上为0.610 mAP），而冻结的Utonia达到0.732。相同架构的随机权重对照模型（0.649和0.652）表明这一提升应归因于预训练（Utonia：+0.080，95%建筑区间 [+0.035, +0.124]）。在所有测试的标注数量下，预训练特征均带来提升……
tldr: 该研究发现冻结的预训练三维点云Transformer（如Utonia）能够编码建筑元素的功能属性（如窗户是否可开启、柱子是否承重），显著优于从头训练的网络和手工描述子，证明预训练是获得建筑功能理解能力的关键。
en_tdlr: Frozen pretrained 3D point transformers (e.g., Utonia) can encode architectural functions such as operable windows and load-bearing columns, significantly outperforming both networks trained from scratch and hand-crafted descriptors, demonstrating that pretraining is key to understanding building functionality.
